components.note: 辛 (bitter) appears twice, one on each side — two bitter parties
讠 (speech) in the middle — a heated exchange of words

example.hanzi: 他们在为这个问题争辩。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài wèi zhège wèntí zhēngbiàn.
example.english: They are arguing about this problem.
example.fact: 辩 is argument in words: 辩论 (debate), 辩护 (to defend in court), 辩解 (to justify), 狡辩 (to quibble). Learners mix it up with 辨 (biàn, to distinguish); 辩 has the speech radical 讠, so it is about talking.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pulling something away by hand
育 sits in the middle; its role in this character is no longer clear
攵 (tap) — a hand-held action, reinforcing the idea of pushing away

example.hanzi: 警察要求大家马上撤离。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá yāoqiú dàjiā mǎshàng chèlí.
example.english: The police asked everyone to evacuate immediately.
example.fact: 撤 means to pull back: 撤退 (retreat), 撤离 (to evacuate), 撤销 (to revoke), 撤职 (to dismiss from a post). In chat apps, 撤回 is the "recall" button that takes back a sent message.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — one of two dogs
讠 (speech) — words in the middle
犬 (dog) — the second dog; two dogs snarling around words suggests a legal dispute

example.pinyin: Tā zài yù zhōng dùguò le sān nián.
example.english: He spent three years in prison.
example.fact: 狱 originally meant a lawsuit, shown by two dogs barking at each other with words between them, and later became "prison." Common words: 监狱 (jail), 入狱 (to be jailed), 越狱 (jailbreak) and 地狱 (hell).

components.note: 钅 (metal) — chains are made of metal
连 (lián) gives the sound — it is close to liàn and also means "to link"

example.pinyin: Tā de xiàngliàn shì jīnzi zuò de.
example.english: Her necklace is made of gold.
example.fact: 链 is a chain: 项链 (necklace), 锁链, 链条. It became productive in modern speech: 产业链 (industry chain), 供应链 (supply chain), 区块链 (blockchain), and 链接 (a web link).

components.note: 尸 is a covering shape here, not "corpse"
由 sits underneath; together they no longer show a clear picture of "session"

example.hanzi: 这是我们学校的第一届运动会。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen xuéxiào de dì yī jiè yùndònghuì.
example.english: This is our school's first sports meet.
example.fact: 届 counts regular events and graduating classes: 第一届, 本届 (this session), 上一届, and 应届毕业生 (this year's graduates). 届时 means "at that time" in formal announcements.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — a warship is a kind of ship
见 (jiàn) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè sōu jūnjiàn hěn dà.
example.english: This warship is very large.
example.fact: 舰 is a naval vessel, counted with 艘: 军舰, 战舰, 航空母舰 (aircraft carrier), 舰队 (fleet). 旗舰 (flagship) has also become a business word, as in 旗舰店 and 旗舰手机.

components.note: 力 (strength) — helping lends strength
且 (qiě) gives only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ bāngzhù wǒ.
example.english: Thank you for helping me.
example.fact: 助 is mostly found in compounds: 帮助, 协助, 助手 (assistant), 助理, 互助 (mutual aid). In sports, 助攻 is an assist. 助 sounds more formal than the everyday verb 帮.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a spacious house gives the sense of width
苋 (xiàn) is the listed sound part, though the match with kuān is weak

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo mǎlù hěn kuān.
example.english: This road is very wide.
example.fact: 宽 describes width (opposite of 窄), but also leniency: 宽容 (tolerant), 宽松 (loose), 放宽 (to relax rules). 宽带 means broadband, and "three meters wide" is 三米宽.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the oldest sense is drying in the sun
共 — the hands (廾) holding the grain out
水 here is a reduced form of 米 (grain), laid out to dry

example.pinyin: Zuótiān xià le yì chǎng bàoyǔ.
example.english: There was a heavy rainstorm yesterday.
example.fact: 暴 means sudden and violent: 暴雨 (downpour), 暴力 (violence), 暴躁 (short-tempered), 暴富 (sudden wealth). The older meaning was exposing grain to the sun, now written 曝 (pù).

components.note: 女 (woman) — the word is for women, usually older ones
波 (bō) gives the sound — close to pó

example.pinyin: Wǒ wàipó zhù zài xiāngxià.
example.english: My grandmother lives in the countryside.
example.fact: 婆 is bound: 外婆 (maternal grandmother), 婆婆 (husband's mother), 婆家 (the husband's family), 老婆 (colloquial "wife"). 婆婆妈妈 describes someone who nags or fusses.

components.note: 石 (stone) — firmness, hardness
角 (jiǎo) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Nǐ quèdìng míngtiān bú xià yǔ ma?
example.english: Are you sure it won't rain tomorrow?
example.fact: 确 appears in compounds for certainty: 确定 (to be sure), 确实 (indeed), 正确 (correct), 准确 (accurate), 明确 (clear), 确认 (to confirm), 确诊 (confirmed diagnosis).

components.note: A picture of a rabbit, with long ears and a short tail shown by the dot

example.pinyin: Tùzi xǐhuan chī húluóbo.
example.english: Rabbits like to eat carrots.
example.fact: 兔 is the fourth animal of the Chinese zodiac. In Chinese folklore a jade rabbit (玉兔) lives on the Moon pounding the elixir of life, which is why Chang'e lunar probes carried a rover named Yutu. Rabbits are counted with 只.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — sweeping is done by hand
彐 is a reduced remnant of 帚 (broom) held in the hand

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ zài jiā dǎsǎo fángjiān.
example.english: On weekends I clean the rooms at home.
example.fact: 扫 is to sweep: 扫地, 打扫 (to clean up), 扫描 (to scan). 扫码 (to scan a QR code) is part of daily payments in China, and 扫兴 means to dampen someone's mood. The noun broom, 扫帚, is read sàozhou.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — an old link to the idea of a solitary animal
虫 (chóng) gives only a loose sound connection

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan dúzì lǚxíng.
example.english: He likes to travel alone.
example.fact: 独 appears in 独立 (independent), 独特 (unique), 独自 (by oneself), 独生子女 (only child). It differs from 孤独 (lonely), which is about the feeling; 独 is mostly about being single or sole.

components.note: 罒 (net) — setting a net down is the old picture of putting things in place
直 (zhí) gives the sound — close to zhì

example.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de wèizhi.
example.english: Please tell me where you are.
example.fact: 置 means to place: 位置 (position), 设置 (settings), 装置 (device), 购置 (to purchase), 闲置 (idle). In chat apps, 置顶 means to pin a conversation to the top.

components.note: 彡 (strokes of decoration) — decorative color and sheen
采 (cǎi) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng biǎoyǎn hěn jīngcǎi.
example.english: This performance is wonderful.
example.fact: 彩 means color and also splendor: 彩色, 彩虹 (rainbow), 精彩 (wonderful, a common compliment). 彩票 is a lottery ticket, so 中彩 means winning the prize; 彩礼 is the bride price.

components.note: 石 (stone) — dishes were once made of stone or pottery
枼 (yè) gives the sound — it is close to dié and suggests something thin and flat

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí ge xiǎo diézi.
example.english: Please give me a small dish.
example.fact: 碟 is a small, flat dish: 碟子, 飞碟 (UFO, "flying saucer"), 光碟 (optical disc). The idiom 小菜一碟 means "a piece of cake," literally "one small side dish."

components.note: 扌 (hand) — breaking is done by hand
斤 (axe) — an axe cutting wood, the old picture of breaking

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de yīfu dǎ bā zhé.
example.english: The clothes in this shop are 20% off.
example.fact: In Chinese discounts, 折 counts what you pay in tenths: 八折 means pay 80%, i.e., 20% off — the opposite of what some learners expect. 折 also means to fold (折纸), to break (折断) and to turn (转折).

components.note: 艹 (plant) — it names a plant
朱 (zhū) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.hanzi: 重阳节人们喜欢插茱萸。
example.pinyin: Chóngyáng Jié rénmen xǐhuan chā zhūyú.
example.english: People like to wear dogwood on the Double Ninth Festival.
example.fact: 茱萸 is a fragrant plant worn on the Double Ninth Festival to ward off evil. Tang poet Wang Wei's line 遍插茱萸少一人 ("everyone puts on dogwood, one person missing") is a famous expression of missing family.

excludeSuggestion: Occurs almost only in 茱萸 and in transliterated names.

components.note: 米 (grain) — the original sense was coarse, unmilled grain
且 (qiě) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Zhè gēn shéngzi hěn cū.
example.english: This rope is very thick.
example.fact: 粗 describes thick round things and coarse textures (opposite of 细): 粗糙 (rough), 粗粮 (whole grains), 粗茶淡饭 (simple food). It also means careless or rude: 粗心 (careless), 粗鲁 (crude).

components.note: 罒 (net) — a covering that goes over something
卓 (zhuó) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Chūmén yào dài kǒuzhào.
example.english: You need to wear a mask when you go out.
example.fact: 罩 is a cover: 口罩 (face mask), 灯罩 (lampshade), 罩衫 (smock). As a verb, it also means to cover or to look after: in slang 我罩你 is "I've got your back."

components.note: 口 — two items, drawn as two squares
丨 (vertical line) — a stick running through them, stringing them together

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī yí chuàn kǎoròu.
example.english: I want to eat a skewer of grilled meat.
example.fact: 串 is a measure word for things strung together: 一串钥匙, 一串葡萄. 羊肉串 (lamb skewers) are a popular street food, and 串门 means to drop in on a neighbour. 串通 means to collude.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — arrow shafts were made of bamboo
前 (qián) gives the sound — a loose match for jiàn

example.pinyin: Tā lā gōng shè chū yì zhī jiàn.
example.english: He drew his bow and shot an arrow.
example.fact: 箭 is counted with 支 or 根. It makes 弓箭 (bow and arrow), 火箭 (rocket, "fire arrow"), 箭头 (arrowhead). The idiom 归心似箭 compares a longing to get home to a flying arrow.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — chewing
爵 (jué) gives the sound — its other reading jué is also used for 嚼

example.pinyin: Chī dōngxi yào xìjiáo mànyàn.
example.english: You should chew your food slowly and thoroughly.
example.fact: 嚼 is to chew, read jiáo in speech and jué in 咀嚼 (jǔjué). 细嚼慢咽 is the standard advice for healthy eating, and 嚼舌根 means to gossip, "chewing the tongue root."

components.note: 几 — the top part, read as a flower or hanging fruit
木 (tree) — a tree with a flower hanging from it

example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ kāi le yì duǒ hóng huā.
example.english: A red flower has bloomed in the garden.
example.fact: 朵 counts flowers and clouds: 一朵花, 一朵云. 花朵 means a blossom, and 耳朵 (ear) also contains 朵, read with a neutral tone: ěrduo.

components.note: 阝 (mound) — the left piece, a hillside or a place
车 (chariot) — chariots drawn up in formation

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn guā le yí zhèn dà fēng.
example.english: A gust of strong wind blew outside.
example.fact: 阵 first meant a battle formation, and still does in 阵容 (lineup) and 上阵 (to go into battle). As a measure word it counts short spells: 一阵风, 一阵雨, 一阵笑声. 一阵子 means "for a while."

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house
佰 (a person and a mat) — someone resting under a roof, per the dictionary reading

example.hanzi: 我们学校的宿舍很干净。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào de sùshè hěn gānjìng.
example.english: The dorm at our school is very clean.
example.fact: 宿 as "to lodge" is read sù: 宿舍 (dormitory), 住宿 (accommodation), 露宿 (to sleep outdoors). It has two other readings: xiǔ, counting nights (一宿), and xiù, in 星宿 (constellation).

components.note: 自 (self) — originally a picture of a nose; people point to their nose to mean "me"
畀 (bì) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, bízi bù tōngqì.
example.english: I have a cold and my nose is blocked.
example.fact: 鼻 is bound in everyday speech as 鼻子. The component 自 is an old picture of a nose, which explains why it came to mean "self." 鼻祖 means a founder, because the nose was thought to form first.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — cheap or lowly, related to money value
戋 (jiān) gives the sound — it matches closely and also suggests "small"

example.pinyin: Bùyào kàn bu qǐ pínjiàn de rén.
example.english: Do not look down on poor and lowly people.
example.fact: 贱 is the opposite of 贵 (expensive; noble), so 贵贱 means high and low. It appears in 低贱, 卑贱 and the polite old self-reference 贱姓 (my humble surname). In slang, 犯贱 means acting annoyingly.

components.note: A hand with a dot marking the pulse point about one cun from the wrist, which gave the unit its name

example.pinyin: Zhè kuài bù yǒu sān cùn kuān.
example.english: This piece of cloth is three cun wide.
example.fact: 寸 is a traditional unit of about 3.3 cm, a bit more than an inch. 英寸 ("English cun") is the word for inch. It also stands for a tiny amount: 寸步难行 (can't take a single step), 一寸光阴一寸金 (time is gold).

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the top part, the plant radical
者 (zhě) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi zhùmíng de zuòjiā.
example.english: He is a famous writer.
example.fact: 著 is formal: 著名 (famous), 著作 (a written work), 名著 (a classic). 四大名著 are the four great classical novels of China. 著 as a verb means to write a book.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earthen walls collapse
夸 (kuā) gives the sound — close to kuǎ

example.hanzi: 那座旧房子被大雨冲垮了。
example.pinyin: Nà zuò jiù fángzi bèi dàyǔ chōng kuǎ le.
example.english: That old house was washed down by the heavy rain.
example.fact: 垮 is to collapse and often follows another verb: 压垮, 累垮 (to be exhausted), 冲垮. 垮台 means to fall from power, and 垮掉的一代 is the Chinese name for the American Beat Generation.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — an emotional state
荒 (huāng) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Bié huāng, mànmàn shuō.
example.english: Don't panic, speak slowly.
example.fact: 慌 is to be flustered: 慌张, 惊慌. After 得, it intensifies unpleasant feelings: 累得慌 (terribly tired), 闷得慌 (bored stiff). This 得慌 pattern is colloquial and only works with negative states.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pinching is done by hand
臽 (xiàn) gives a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 她掐了我一下，我吓了一跳。
example.pinyin: Tā qiā le wǒ yíxià, wǒ xià le yí tiào.
example.english: She pinched me and I jumped.
example.fact: 掐 is pinching with fingers or nails: 掐断 (to cut off), 掐死 (to strangle). 掐指一算 describes counting on one's fingers like a fortune-teller. It is also used for picking flowers: 掐花.

components.note: 石 (stone) — grinding was done with stone mills
麻 (má) gives the sound — close to mó

example.pinyin: Wǒ yòng kāfēijī mó kāfēidòu.
example.english: I grind coffee beans with a coffee machine.
example.fact: 磨 is to grind or rub: 磨刀 (to sharpen a knife), 折磨 (to torment), 磨练 (to temper), 磨蹭 (to dawdle). As a noun the millstone is read mò: 石磨. The proverb 铁杵磨成针 means perseverance works.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — an old sense is a cut or wound
仓 (cāng) is the listed sound part, though the match with chuàng is loose

example.pinyin: Tā chuànglì le yì jiā xiǎo gōngsī.
example.english: He founded a small company.
example.fact: 创 is "to create" in 创造, 创新 (innovation), 创业 (to start a business), 创作 (to create works). It has another reading, chuāng, for wounds: 创伤 (trauma) and 创可贴 (band-aid).

components.note: 木 (tree) — the old sense was the tip of a tree
示 stands in for 票 (piào) of traditional 標, which gave the sound

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài dìtú shàng biāochū wèizhi.
example.english: Please mark the location on the map.
example.fact: 标 originally meant a tree-top, then a mark. It builds 目标 (goal), 标准 (standard), 标题 (title), 标签 (label), 招标 (to invite bids). 标 can also be a verb: 标出, 标明.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — a bird of prey

example.pinyin: Yì zhī yīng zài tiānkōng zhōng fēi.
example.english: An eagle is flying in the sky.
example.fact: 鹰 is counted with 只. 老鹰 is the everyday word, and 老鹰捉小鸡 ("the eagle catches the chicks") is a popular children's game. 雄鹰 means a mighty eagle, and 鹰派 is a hawk in politics.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — repeated twice, as if chanting a spell
几 — the bottom part, not clearly meaningful today

example.pinyin: Mófǎshī niàn le yí jù zhòuyǔ.
example.english: The magician recited a spell.
example.fact: 咒 is a spell or curse: 咒语, 念咒 (to chant a spell), 诅咒 (to curse). 紧箍咒, the headband spell that controls the Monkey King in Journey to the West, is now a metaphor for a rule that keeps you in check.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a liquid action
西 (xī) gives only a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 不小心把水洒在桌子上了。
example.pinyin: Bù xiǎoxīn bǎ shuǐ sǎ zài zhuōzi shàng le.
example.english: I accidentally spilled water on the table.
example.fact: 洒 is used for liquids (洒水, 洒泪), while 撒 (sǎ) is for solids like seeds or salt. 洒脱 and 潇洒 describe a free and easy style. Do not mix it up with 酒 (jiǔ, alcohol).

components.note: 夂 — a downward-foot shape, suggesting movement
田 (field) — the dictionary reads going out to the field to prepare for harvest

example.hanzi: 明天要考试，我今晚要准备一下。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān yào kǎoshì, wǒ jīnwǎn yào zhǔnbèi yíxià.
example.english: There is an exam tomorrow, so I need to prepare tonight.
example.fact: 备 is to prepare: 准备, 预备, 备课 (to prepare a lesson), 设备 (equipment), 备份 (backup), 备注 (a note field on a form). It is a simplified form of 備.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — the old word named a kind of bird, apparently a crow
牙 (yá) gives the sound — close to yǎ

example.pinyin: Tā de jǔzhǐ hěn wényǎ.
example.english: His manners are very refined.
example.fact: 雅 means elegant: 文雅, 优雅, 高雅, 雅致 (tasteful). The elegant sense is a loan; the character first named a bird. 雅思 is how IELTS is written in Chinese, and 雅座 means a private booth in a restaurant.

components.note: A stylized animal: horns on top, eyes, nose and mouth stacked below

example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu hěn duō yěshòu.
example.english: There are many wild beasts in the forest.
example.fact: 兽 refers to four-legged beasts: 野兽 (wild animal), 怪兽 (monster), 兽医 (veterinarian). 禽兽 (birds and beasts) is an insult for a brutal person, and 衣冠禽兽 describes a well-dressed scoundrel.

components.note: 尸 is a covering shape here, not "corpse"
衣 (clothes) — spreading out garments, the old picture of laying things out to view

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù kàn yìshù zhǎn.
example.english: This weekend we are going to see an art exhibition.
example.fact: 展 means to spread out: 展开 (unfold), 展示 (display), 发展 (develop), 进展 (progress), 展望 (outlook). On its own it often means an exhibition: 画展 (art show), 车展 (auto show).

components.note: 钅 (metal) — metal and money suggest trade and shops
甫 (fǔ) gives the sound — a near match for pū

example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ chuáng pū hǎo.
example.english: Please help me make the bed.
example.fact: 铺 is pū as a verb (铺床 make a bed, 铺路 pave a road, 铺垫 lay groundwork) and pù as a noun for a shop or bed: 店铺, 床铺. 铺张 means extravagant.

components.note: A simplified form of 盧, an old word for a vessel; the strokes no longer picture anything

example.pinyin: Lú xiānsheng shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
example.english: Mr. Lu is my teacher.
example.fact: 卢 is a surname and a transliteration character: 卢浮宫 (the Louvre), 卢森堡 (Luxembourg), 卢布 (rouble). 卢沟桥 is the Marco Polo Bridge outside Beijing.

excludeSuggestion: Used almost only as a surname or in transliterations of foreign names.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — cooling and shrinking
咸 (xián) gives only a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 我想减肥，所以少吃甜食。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jiǎnféi, suǒyǐ shǎo chī tiánshí.
example.english: I want to lose weight, so I eat less sweets.
example.fact: 减 is the opposite of 加: 减少 (to reduce), 减肥 (to lose weight), 减价 (price cut), 减速 (to slow down), and 减法 (subtraction). 加减乘除 are the four arithmetic operations.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — yielding, stepping aside
孙 (sūn) gives the sound — close to xùn

example.hanzi: 他的成绩比我稍逊一筹。
example.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì bǐ wǒ shāo xùn yì chóu.
example.english: His grades are slightly below mine.
example.fact: 逊 means "inferior" or "modest": 逊色 (to be less impressive), 毫不逊色 (just as good), 谦逊 (humble), 出言不逊 (to speak rudely). It can also mean to abdicate: 逊位.

components.note: 页 (head) — the forehead is part of the head
客 (kè) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā de étóu shàng yǒu yí dào bā.
example.english: He has a scar on his forehead.
example.fact: 额 is the forehead (额头) and also a fixed amount: 金额 (sum), 名额 (quota), 余额 (balance), 额外 (extra).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — moving things by hand
那 (nà) gives the sound — a near match for nuó

example.hanzi: 请把椅子往旁边挪一下。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yǐzi wǎng pángbiān nuó yíxià.
example.english: Please move the chair over a bit.
example.fact: 挪 moves something a short distance: 挪动, 挪一挪. 挪用 means to misappropriate funds (挪用公款), and 挪窝 is colloquial for moving house. 挪威 is Norway.
